The antiderivatives of some functions, like sin (x2), 1>ln x, and 21 + x4, have no ele- mentary formulas. When we cannot find a workable antiderivative for a function ƒ that we have to integrate, we can partition the interval of integration, replace ƒ by a closely fitting polynomial on each subinterval, integrate the polynomials, and add the results to approxi- mate the definite integral of ƒ.
